A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same prototype-decoupling research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, allowing retained, revised and newly added content to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original prototype-collapse measurements, training-dynamics experiments, ImageNet and iNaturalist evaluations, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds transfer evaluations, computational measurements, scheduler ablations and experiments adapting decoupling to DINO.

M1.justification: The core online-GMM updates, responsibility-weighted forgetting, annealing and split-resurrect procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds a DINO-specific adaptation that replaces centering with Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization and changes teacher-temperature scheduling, modifying the procedure used for that framework.

E1.justification: v2 retains ImageNet-1k and iNaturalist2018 and adds transfer evaluation across eight datasets: Aircr, C101, Cars, Flower, Food, Pets, SUN397 and VOC2007 (Table 4). This substantially broadens evaluation across image-recognition domains beyond the original coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds CARP + KP as a comparator in the iNaturalist comparison and the ImageNet ViT-S/16 comparisons. Tables 3 and C.1 also add plain CARP at 300 epochs with ViT-S/16, supplying a matched backbone/budget baseline previously absent from those comparisons. Existing comparator families are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include transfer evaluation following Ericsson et al., memory measurements across global batch sizes 128–2048, and controlled DINO experiments varying normalization, temperature and prototype count. Reported GMM settings also change: v1 assigns the linear 0.1–0.5 schedule to forgetting factor eta; v2 assigns it to smoothing factor beta and describes a separate eta schedule in Appendix A.2. This establishes a reporting revision, not that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The original component ablation is retained. v2 adds forgetting-schedule sensitivity tests (Table A.2), extensive DINO stabilization ablations involving centering, Sinkhorn-Knopp, temperature and prototype count (Table C.3), and computational-cost analysis. Figures 3–4 also extend the collapse and training-dynamics analyses to DINO + Decoupling.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 newly discloses that the modified DINO data loader prevents reuse of the original data-loading seed. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The change concerns seed information, without establishing additional runs or improved uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Most existing tabulated scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 2 newly reports DINO + Decoupling at 36.2% overall versus DINO's 45.3%, and CARP + KP at 45.3% versus CARP's 45.9%. New tables report transfer, sensitivity and resource results, including 37.9 versus 38.1 training hours. Figure 3 also corrects the CARP/DINOv2 curve assignments: their approximately 11%/43% uniqueness at epsilon 0.025 now agrees with Table 1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix C.1's weighted-centroid lemma, non-collapse proposition, fixed-point corollary and proofs; v1 has no corresponding theoretical development. However, Proposition C.2 incorrectly infers different normalized weights from different raw responsibility columns. Distinct proportional columns yield identical centroids, undermining the proposition as stated.

C1.justification: The central diagnosis of joint optimization and the proposed decoupling contribution remain. The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion narrow downstream-performance claims: improvements now occur in several settings, and robustness benefits vary across architectures, replacing the earlier broadly consistent-benefit framing.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies the relationship between prototype diversity and performance. It discusses DINO instability and failed transfer of tuned settings to iNaturalist, limited transfer-learning gains, and framework-dependent KP tuning. New limitations address nonadaptive prototype tracking, added hyperparameters and Gaussian assumptions for normalized features. Appendix C.3 proposes architectural explanations for CARP's greater stability.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code link, MI250X hardware information, training-time measurements, explicit 300-epoch training information for the iNaturalist comparison, and DINO data-loader/mixed-precision details. The existing CARP hyperparameter table is retained. Scheduler documentation expands, although Equation A.7 conflicts with its stated initial eta value.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cuturi (2013) for Sinkhorn normalization and Ericsson et al. (2021) for transfer evaluation, while removing Wu et al. (2025). It also positions complete collapse removal as complementary to earlier partial mitigation. Most research positioning is retained; publication-metadata updates and changed year-letter assignments do not introduce new works.

P1.justification: The main six-section narrative remains recognizable, with targeted introductory clarification and substantial local rewriting of the long-tailed-results discussion. Appendix C becomes Extended Results, nesting the retained linear-evaluation material under C.2. Acknowledgments, an LLM-use declaration and conference/author formatting are added; most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds five tables: transfer, memory, runtime, scheduler sensitivity and DINO sensitivity. Figures 3–4 gain DINO + Decoupling curves and revised legends/colors, and Figure 4 moves alongside Figure 3. Existing comparison tables gain rows, while appendix tables are condensed and reformatted. These substantially expand and reorganize the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical scrutiny through matched CARP controls, DINO failure analysis, transfer/resource evaluations and appropriately narrowed performance claims. However, its newly added non-collapse proposition fails for proportional responsibility columns, and the printed forgetting schedule gives an initial eta near 1.09 despite claiming 0.89. These introduced problems affect mathematical soundness and reproducibility. The substantial empirical benefits and new technical defects prevent a reliable judgment of the net quality direction.
